exploracion.desc: How each column is spread and which columns move together, with a written summary checked against the numbers. It changes and chooses nothing.
exploracion.ayuda: Every figure in the summary comes from your table, recomputed separately. It is a check of the text, not a conclusion about your data.
exploracion.no_cuadro: The written summary did not match the numbers, so it is not shown; the tables below are the ones that count.

resumen.columnas: Your table has {filas} rows. Numeric columns: {numericas}; categorical: {categoricas}.
resumen.sesgadas: Heavily skewed (almost all values on one side and a few far away): {lista}.
resumen.sin_sesgadas: No numeric column is heavily skewed.
resumen.pareja: The two numeric columns that move together the most: {par} (r = {r}; {sentido}).

sentido.contrario: when one rises, the other falls

resumen.sin_pareja: No pair of numeric columns clearly moves together.
resumen.cramer: Among the categorical columns, the strongest association is {par} (Cramér’s V {v}).
resumen.aviso: Two columns moving together does not mean one causes the other.

matriz.titulo: Correlation between numeric columns (Pearson, from −1 to 1)
matriz.ayuda: Close to 1: they rise and fall together. Close to −1: when one rises, the other falls. Close to 0: they do not move together in a straight line. “–” means there are not enough rows with both.
matriz.recortada: The first {max} numeric columns of {total} are shown.
matriz.sin: There are fewer than two numeric columns: no correlations to show.

cramer.titulo: Association between categorical columns (Cramér’s V, from 0 to 1)
cramer.sin: There are no two categorical columns with between 2 and 20 categories to associate.
